Company Profile: Reliance Industries Limited (NSE/BSE: RELIANCE)
Business Overview: Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) is India's largest corporate conglomerate by market capitalization and revenue. Operates market-leading businesses across Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C refining & petrochemicals), Retail (Reliance Retail), Digital Services (Jio Platforms), and New Energy (solar, hydrogen, energy storage gigafactories in Jamnagar).
Core Operating Segments: 1. Oil-to-Chemicals (O2C): Jamnagar complex with 1.24 million barrels/day refining capacity; 2. Digital Services (Jio): 490M+ subscribers, world's largest 5G standalone network, ARPU INR 195.1; 3. Reliance Retail: 18,900+ stores with INR 75,000+ Cr quarterly gross revenue; 4. Oil & Gas E&P: KG D6 deepwater gas producing 30 MMSCMD (accounting for ~30% of India's domestic gas production).
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated Q2 FY25 revenue at INR 2,35,481 Cr, quarterly EBITDA at INR 43,934 Cr, and PAT at INR 19,323 Cr. Shareholders' net worth exceeds INR 7,94,900 Cr. Net debt to EBITDA remains prudent at ~0.65x. Approved 1:1 bonus equity share issue in October 2024, expanding retail investor base.
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Regulated under Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) pricing formulas for KG-D6 gas, Department of Telecommunications (DoT) spectrum usage charges and license fees, and Ministry of Finance windfall profit taxes on fuel exports.
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: INR 75,000 Cr committed capex in Dhirubhai Ambani Green Energy Giga Complex (solar PV, energy storage, green hydrogen electrolysers). Accelerating 5G monetization, enterprise cloud partnerships with NVIDIA/Google, and planned value-unlocking listings of Jio and Retail.

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Pioneered hyper-local delivery in India with an integrated consumer ecosystem covering Food Delivery, Quick Commerce (Instamart), Out-of-Home consumption (Dineout), and on-demand delivery (Genie). Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Cash and liquid investments exceed INR 5,800 Cr, ensuring a multi-year cash runway with zero net debt. Quick commerce adjusted EBITDA margin is approaching breakeven (-3.2% of GOV vs -8.9% YoY).
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. INR 703 Cr earmarked for supply chain infrastructure, cold storage, and dark store robotic automation. INR 1,115 Cr dedicated to technology and cloud infrastructure. Key catalyst: dark-store density leading to sub-10 minute deliveries.

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. The current momentum in silver is supported by a structural shift in industrial demand rather than speculative retail froth. The conviction score of 86/100 reflects a STRONG_ACCUMULATE stance. This rating is derived from the convergence of supply-side deficits and the current volatility profile. For fresh capital deployment, the strategy is to treat the current price levels as a primary entry zone. The basket is designed to capture the upside of physical bullion while maintaining the liquidity of exchange-traded instruments.

The portfolio exhibits a 1-year 95% Parametric VaR of -18.4% and a Conditional VaR of -27.6%. The 5-year Bearish Support Floor (P10) at ₹20.81 is a critical stress-test metric. This figure represents a scenario where high volatility diffusion drag effectively neutralizes the expected drift during a prolonged cyclical stagnation. While the baseline P50 target of ₹39.57 assumes a healthy recovery, the P10 floor accounts for the reality that silver is a high-beta commodity; in a severe downcycle, the cost of carry and volatility decay can compress returns toward the initial capital entry point, even if the underlying physical asset maintains some value.

STRUCTURAL CATALYSTS & VALUATION:
The valuation is underpinned by three primary drivers:
• Industrial Solar PV Demand: Silver consumption in photovoltaic cells continues to outpace supply, creating a structural deficit.
• Physical Deficit: Global mine production remains inelastic, failing to meet the combined demand of industrial manufacturing and investment hedging.

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

The quantitative assessment of Tata Motors under a 2x macro volatility shock indicates a significant expansion in tail-risk exposure. Under baseline conditions, the position is projected to grow from the initial capital base to a terminal value of ₹1,927,150.96 over a 5-year horizon. However, a 2x volatility shock effectively doubles the standard deviation, widening the distribution of outcomes. The 95% Parametric VaR of -29.7% suggests that in a single-year stress event, the portfolio faces a potential loss of ₹297,000. The 95% Conditional VaR (CVaR) of -41.5% quantifies the expected loss in the tail of the distribution, representing a potential drawdown of ₹415,000 during extreme market dislocation.

PORTFOLIO CONVICTION & POSTURE:
The 88/100 conviction score reflects a STRONG_ACCUMULATE posture. This rating is driven by the company's transition toward high-margin EV segments and deleveraging of the JLR balance sheet. For fresh capital deployment, the current valuation provides a sufficient margin of safety to absorb short-term volatility. The strategy for this deployment is to treat the current price as an entry point for long-term compounding, prioritizing the 5-year terminal value over interim price fluctuations.

QUANTITATIVE VOLATILITY & DOWNSIDE VAR:
The historical volatility of 28.5% is elevated, reflecting the cyclical nature of the automotive sector. The 5-Year Bearish Floor (P10) at ₹620.11 represents a scenario where the compounding effect is neutralized by prolonged cyclical stagnation. In this stress scenario, the high volatility diffusion drag—where large percentage swings require disproportionate gains to recover—offsets the underlying drift. This contrasts sharply with the P50 median projection of ₹1,410.00, which assumes a mean-reversion to the long-term growth trend. The maximum drawdown floor of 46.0% serves as the historical boundary for risk management, implying that investors must be prepared for significant interim paper losses during macro-economic contractions.

STRUCTURAL CATALYSTS & VALUATION:
The investment thesis rests on three primary pillars:
• Operating Cash Flow: Sustained improvement in JLR free cash flow generation, which is critical for debt reduction.
• ROE Expansion: Expected improvement in Return on Equity as the product mix shifts toward higher-margin luxury and electric vehicles.
• DCF Drivers: The terminal value is supported by a robust pipeline of new product launches and a reduction in capital expenditure intensity as the EV platform matures.

STATUTORY TAX DRAG & NET IN-HAND WEALTH:
Applying the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, the gross final wealth of ₹1,927,150.96 is subject to a 12.5% LTCG tax on gains exceeding the ₹1.25 Lakh threshold. Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Pioneered hyper-local delivery in India with an integrated consumer ecosystem covering Food Delivery, Quick Commerce (Instamart), Out-of-Home consumption (Dineout), and on-demand delivery (Genie). Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Cash and liquid investments exceed INR 5,800 Cr, ensuring a multi-year cash runway with zero net debt. Quick commerce adjusted EBITDA margin is approaching breakeven (-3.2% of GOV vs -8.9% YoY).
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. INR 703 Cr earmarked for supply chain infrastructure, cold storage, and dark store robotic automation. INR 1,115 Cr dedicated to technology and cloud infrastructure. Key catalyst: dark-store density leading to sub-10 minute deliveries.

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

output.executive_synthesis:
DIRECT INQUIRY RESOLUTION:
Reliance Industries represents a core compounding vehicle for a 5-year horizon. Based on current market pricing of 1324.4, the quantitative model projects a median terminal value of 2,448,030 from your initial 1,000,000 deployment. This represents a 13.07% CAGR, significantly outperforming the 5.49% inflation benchmark with a 78.2% probability of success. The investment is characterized by high liquidity and institutional-grade stability, making it suitable for long-term wealth accumulation despite cyclical energy sector sensitivities.

PORTFOLIO CONVICTION & POSTURE:
The conviction score of 84/100 reflects a high-confidence outlook tempered by the necessity of price discipline. The ACCUMULATE_STAGGERED directive is mandatory because Reliance exhibits a volatility profile of 19.5%, which can lead to significant short-term variance. For your fresh 1,000,000 capital, a lump-sum entry exposes the portfolio to unnecessary timing risk. Staggered deployment mitigates the impact of the 34.5% historical maximum drawdown, ensuring that your average cost basis remains optimized against the P50 median trajectory.

QUANTITATIVE VOLATILITY & DOWNSIDE VAR:
The risk profile is defined by a 1-year 95% Parametric VaR of -17.9%, indicating that in a 1-in-20 year event, the portfolio could experience a drawdown of this magnitude within a single year. The 95% Conditional VaR of -26.0% accounts for tail-risk events. The P10 Bearish Floor of 1,395,480 is a critical metric; it models a scenario where high volatility diffusion drag effectively cancels out the underlying drift of the business. In this stress scenario, the capital barely preserves its real value over 5 years. This contrasts sharply with the P50 median of 2,448,030, highlighting that while the upside is robust, the investor must be prepared for periods of stagnation if macroeconomic conditions suppress the O2C (Oil to Chemicals) and retail margins simultaneously.

STRUCTURAL CATALYSTS & VALUATION:
Reliance is currently transitioning from a traditional energy-heavy conglomerate to a technology and retail-led ecosystem. Key drivers include the scaling of digital services, the expansion of retail footprint, and the long-term transition toward green energy infrastructure. These segments provide a hedge against the cyclicality of the refining business. ROE remains supported by strong operating cash flows, which are essential for funding the high capital expenditure requirements of the next 5 years. The valuation is supported by the company's ability to maintain market leadership across diverse, high-barrier-to-entry sectors.

STATUTORY TAX DRAG & NET IN-HAND WEALTH:
Under the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, your gross terminal wealth of 1,848,406.83 is subject to a 12.5% LTCG tax on gains exceeding the 1.25 lakh threshold. After accounting for the 0.1% delivery STT and the applicable capital gains tax, your net post-tax CAGR is 11.9%. This results in a net in-hand wealth of approximately 1,766,000 after all statutory obligations are met at the end of the 5-year term.

PERSONALIZED ACTION BLUEPRINT:
To deploy your 1,000,000 capital effectively for wealth compounding, follow this staggered entry protocol:
• Phase 1: Deploy 300,000 immediately to establish a baseline position.
• Phase 2: Allocate the remaining 700,000 into a liquid fund or high-yield sweep account.
• Phase 3: Execute 100,000 tranches every quarter or upon a 5% correction from your average entry price, whichever occurs first.
• Phase 4: Maintain this discipline for 18 months to complete the full deployment. This approach lowers your volatility exposure and aligns with the ACCUMULATE_STAGGERED mandate, ensuring you do not exhaust your capital during a temporary market dip.

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 — Regulation 30: Every listed entity shall promptly make disclosures of any events or information which, in the opinion of the board of directors, are material. Material events under Schedule III Part A must be disclosed to recognized stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) as soon as reasonably possible and no later than: (a) thirty minutes from the closure of the board meeting for outcome disclosures; (b) twelve hours from occurrence for events originating within the entity; (c) twenty-four hours from occurrence for external events.

Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Pioneered hyper-local delivery in India with an integrated consumer ecosystem covering Food Delivery, Quick Commerce (Instamart), Out-of-Home consumption (Dineout), and on-demand delivery (Genie). Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Cash and liquid investments exceed INR 5,800 Cr, ensuring a multi-year cash runway with zero net debt. Quick commerce adjusted EBITDA margin is approaching breakeven (-3.2% of GOV vs -8.9% YoY).
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. INR 703 Cr earmarked for supply chain infrastructure, cold storage, and dark store robotic automation. INR 1,115 Cr dedicated to technology and cloud infrastructure. The RBI monetary policy corridor, anchored at a 6.50 percent repo rate, exerts structural pressure on HDFC Bank by elevating the cost of funds. Simultaneously, the Finance Act 2024 revision to Securities Transaction Tax (STT) on equity delivery trades increases the friction cost for institutional rebalancing. For a 5-year horizon, this creates a dual-headwind: margin contraction limits earnings growth, while higher transaction costs dampen the velocity of institutional accumulation. Despite these factors, the bank's ability to reprice its loan book toward high-yield retail segments provides a buffer, supporting a projected 5-year terminal value of ₹1,516.13 from the current entry point.

The 84/100 conviction score reflects a high-quality asset currently undergoing a valuation reset. The 95 percent Conditional VaR of -23.0 percent highlights the tail risk associated with systemic banking sector shocks. retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

retrieved_evidence.title: Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-CAPITAL-GAINS" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Capital Gains Restructuring (12.5% LTCG & 20% STCG)
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter IV amendments to Section 112A and Section 111A of the Income-tax Act, 1961: 1. Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) on listed equity shares, equity-oriented units, and business trust units held > 12 months are taxed at 12.5% (increased from 10%) for transfers on or after July 23, 2024. The annual aggregate LTCG exemption limit under Section 112A was increased from INR 1,00,000 to INR 1,25,000. 2. Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG) under Section 111A on listed equities held <= 12 months are taxed at 20% (increased from 15%). Indexation benefit on unlisted assets and real estate is rationalized to 12.5% without indexation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>

Material events under Schedule III Part A must be disclosed to recognized stock exchanges (NSE/BSE) as soon as reasonably possible and no later than: (a) thirty minutes from the closure of the board meeting for outcome disclosures; (b) twelve hours from occurrence for events originating within the entity; (c) twenty-four hours from occurrence for external events.

Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.

Company Profile: Swiggy Limited (NSE/BSE: SWIGGY)
Business Overview: Swiggy Limited is one of India's leading consumer tech on-demand convenience platforms. Pioneered hyper-local delivery in India with an integrated consumer ecosystem covering Food Delivery, Quick Commerce (Instamart), Out-of-Home consumption (Dineout), and on-demand delivery (Genie). Listed on NSE and BSE on November 13, 2024, successfully raising INR 11,327 crore in India's second-largest tech IPO of 2024.
Core Operating Segments: 1. Food Delivery: Gross Order Value (GOV) exceeding INR 24,000 Cr annualized with ~14M average monthly transacting users (MTUs). Take rate stands at 23.5%-24.0% with positive contribution margin of ~6.8% of GOV. 2. Quick Commerce (Instamart): Rapidly scaling dark-store network with 605+ active dark stores across 43 Indian cities. Instamart GOV reached INR 8,500+ Cr annualized growing 86% YoY. Average order value (AOV) is INR 485. 3. Out-of-Home & Supply Chain: Dineout restaurant reservations & table payments, plus Scootsy warehouse operations.
Key Financial Highlights: Consolidated quarterly revenue from operations reached INR 3,601.5 Cr in Q2 FY25. Post-IPO net worth stands at INR 9,250 Cr, bolstered by fresh issue proceeds. Cash and liquid investments exceed INR 5,800 Cr, ensuring a multi-year cash runway with zero net debt. Quick commerce adjusted EBITDA margin is approaching breakeven (-3.2% of GOV vs -8.9% YoY).
Regulatory & Tax Considerations: Subject to SEBI LODR quarterly reporting obligations, DPIIT Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) ecommerce marketplace guidelines, and state-level gig worker welfare legislation (Karnataka, Rajasthan Gig Worker welfare boards). No foreign direct ownership of grocery inventory (strictly operates marketplace model with dark-store merchant partners).
Strategic Capex & Growth Catalysts: Planned Capex of INR 1,178 Cr from IPO proceeds for expanding Instamart dark store footprint from 605 to over 1,000 stores by FY26. INR 703 Cr earmarked for supply chain infrastructure, cold storage, and dark store robotic automation. INR 1,115 Cr dedicated to technology and cloud infrastructure. Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DELIVERY" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) Equity Delivery
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Chapter VII — Securities Transaction Tax: Under Section 98 and Section 99, taxable securities transactions in Equity Delivery on recognized stock exchanges shall be levied at 0.1% (one-tenth of one percent) payable by both the purchaser and seller. For equity intraday (non-delivery) transactions, the statutory rate is 0.025% payable by the seller only. Statutory costs are mandatory and deduct from gross trading turnover before net trading realization.
